content: On Saturday, March 29, 2014, the following interviews and discussions are scheduled: At 10:00 AM, Dr. P.J. Devereaux will discuss the effects of acetyl-salicylic acid (aspirin) on major arterial and venous complications in patients undergoing noncardiac surgery. The embargo on this information will be lifted on Monday, March 31, 2014, at 8:00 AM. At 10:30 AM, Dr. Nadia Bandstein will present findings on the prognostic implications of negative high-sensitivity troponin levels in emergency department patients and their associated risk of myocardial infarction. The embargo will be lifted on Sunday, March 30, 2014, at 11:45 AM. At 2:30 PM, Dr. Jennifer Robinson will discuss the results of a Phase 3, double-blind, randomized trial evaluating the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of evolocumab (a PCSK9 monoclonal antibody) in combination with statin therapy for patients with primary hypercholesterolemia and mixed dyslipidemia. The embargo will be lifted on Sunday, March 30, 2014, at 8:15 AM. At 3:00 PM, Dr. Marco Valgimigli will present a randomized controlled trial comparing bare-metal stents to zotarolimus-eluting stents in patients who are uncertain candidates for drug-eluting stents. The embargo will be lifted on Monday, March 31, 2014, at 11:30 AM. At 3:30 PM, Dr. A. Michael Lincoff will discuss the AleCardio trial, which evaluated the dual PPAR-α/γ agonist aleglitazar for reducing cardiovascular events in patients with acute coronary syndrome and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The embargo will be lifted on Monday, March 31, 2014, at 11:30 AM. At 4:00 PM, Dr. Ajay Kirtane will provide a daily wrap-up of the ACC conference in English. On Sunday, March 30, 2014, the following events are planned: At 12:30 PM, Dr. Masahiro Natsuaki will present the two-year outcomes of a trial comparing second-generation drug-eluting stents with biodegradable versus durable polymers. This is part of the NEXT trial. The embargo will be lifted on Sunday, March 30, 2014, at 8:45 AM. At 1:00 PM, Dr. Anders Bruun Mathiasen and Professor Jens Kastrup will discuss the MSC-HF trial, which investigated autotransplantation of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells in patients with severe ischemic heart failure. The embargo will be lifted on Monday, March 31, 2014, at 11:45 AM. At 1:30 PM, Dr. Rogerio Sarmentio-Leite will provide a wrap-up of the ACC conference in Portuguese. At 2:00 PM, Dr. Basil Lewis will provide a wrap-up of the ACC conference in Hebrew. At 2:30 PM, Dr. Ilan Goldenberg will discuss long-term survival outcomes associated with cardiac resynchronization therapy in patients with mild heart failure. The embargo will be lifted on Sunday, March 30, 2014, at 11:45 AM. At 3:30 PM, Dr. Roxana Mehran will provide a wrap-up of the ACC conference in English. At 4:00 PM, Dr. Ajay Kirtane will again provide a wrap-up of the ACC conference in English. On Monday, March 31, 2014, the following sessions are scheduled: At 8:00 AM, Dr. Deepak Bhatt will present the main results of the SYMPLICITY HTN-3 trial. The embargo will be lifted on Saturday, March 29, 2014, at 9:35 AM. At 8:30 AM, Dr. Stefan James will provide a wrap-up of the ACC conference from a Scandinavian perspective. At 9:00 AM, Dr. David Adams will discuss a randomized comparison of self-expanding transcatheter and surgical aortic valve replacement in high-risk patients with severe aortic stenosis. The embargo will be lifted on Saturday, March 29, 2014, at 9:10 AM. At 10:00 AM, Dr. Massimo Imazio will present the results of the CORP-2 trial, a multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled study evaluating the efficacy and safety of colchicine in patients with multiple recurrences of pericarditis. The embargo will be lifted on Sunday, March 30, 2014, at 10:45 AM. At 10:30 AM, Dr. Aimee Armstrong will discuss the one-year follow-up results of the Melody Transcatheter Pulmonary Valve Multicenter Post-Approval Study. The embargo will be lifted on Sunday, March 30, 2014, at 11:15 AM. At 11:00 AM, Dr. Phillip Raymond Schauer will present the three-year results of the STAMPEDE trial, which compared bariatric surgery to intensive medical therapy for long-term glycemic control and diabetes complications. The embargo will be lifted on Monday, March 31, 2014, at 9:00 AM. At 11:30 AM, Dr. Ajay Kirtane will provide a wrap-up of the ACC conference in English. At 12:00 PM, Dr. Hisao Ogawa and Dr. Tomohiro Sakamoto will provide a wrap-up of the ACC conference in Japanese. At 12:30 PM, Dr. Richard Whitlock will discuss the SIRS trial, which evaluated the use of steroids in cardiac surgery. The embargo will be lifted on Monday, March 31, 2014, at 8:30 AM. At 1:00 PM, Dr. Gennaro Sardella will provide a wrap-up of the ACC conference in Italian. At 1:30 PM, Dr. Daniel Sessler will present the results of a large international trial assessing the effects of clonidine on major arterial events in patients undergoing noncardiac surgery. The embargo will be lifted on Monday, March 31, 2014, at 8:15 AM. At 2:00 PM, Dr. Juan Gaspar will provide a wrap-up of the ACC conference in Spanish. At 2:30 PM, Dr. Freek Verheugt will provide a wrap-up of the ACC conference in Dutch. At 3:00 PM, Dr. Mohamed Abdel-Wahab will present the CHOICE trial, a randomized comparison of self-expandable and balloon-expandable prostheses in patients undergoing transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement. The embargo will be lifted on Sunday, March 30, 2014, at 8:00 AM. At 3:30 PM, Dr. Gilles Montalescot will provide a wrap-up of the ACC conference in French. At 4:00 PM, Dr. David Holmes will discuss one-year outcomes from the STS/ACC Transcatheter Valve Therapy (TVT) Registry. The embargo will be lifted on Monday, March 31, 2014, at 10:45 AM. At 4:30 PM, Dr. Chris Lexis will present findings on the use of metformin in acute myocardial infarction. The embargo will be lifted on Monday, March 31, 2014, at 8:45 AM. At 5:00 PM, Dr. Adeel Shahzad and Dr. Rod Stables will discuss a unique randomized controlled trial comparing unfractionated heparin to bivalirudin in primary percutaneous coronary intervention. The embargo will be lifted on Monday, March 31, 2014, at 12:30 PM. At 5:20 PM, Professor Harvey White will present the STABILITY trial, which evaluated the inhibition of lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A2 with darapladib in patients with chronic coronary heart disease. He will also provide a wrap-up of the ACC conference from the Pacific Rim perspective. The embargo will be lifted on Sunday, March 30, 2014, at 8:00 AM. On Tuesday, April 1, 2014, the following is scheduled: At 9:00 AM, Dr. Sigmund Silber will provide a wrap-up of the ACC conference in German.
